title: Omega-3 and DHA in Pregnancy: Food Sources and Supplement Cautions
excerpt: Why DHA matters for fetal development, low-mercury fish options, and when to ask a clinician about supplements
content:
## Introduction to Omega-3 and DHA in Pregnancy
Omega-3 and DHA are essential nutrients for fetal development. DHA (Docosahexaenoic acid) is a type of omega-3 fatty acid that plays a crucial role in the development of the fetal brain and eyes.

## Role of DHA in Pregnancy
DHA supports the development of the fetal brain and eyes, as well as the development of the immune system. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), DHA may also help reduce the risk of preterm birth and other pregnancy-related complications.

## Food Sources of Omega-3 and DHA
There are many food sources rich in Omega-3 and DHA, including:
* Fatty fish like salmon and sardines
* Shellfish like mussels and oysters
* Nuts and seeds like walnuts and flaxseeds
* Fortified foods like eggs and yogurt

## Precautions when Consuming Fish during Pregnancy
While fish is a rich source of Omega-3 and DHA, it's essential to be cautious when consuming fish during pregnancy. Fish can contain mercury, a toxic substance that can harm fetal development. According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), pregnant women should limit their consumption of high-mercury fish like shark and swordfish.

## Omega-3 and DHA Supplements during Pregnancy
Omega-3 and DHA supplements can be a good option for pregnant women who cannot get enough of these nutrients from food sources. However, not all supplements are created equal. Look for supplements that contain DHA and EPA (Eicosapentaenoic acid), and consult with your healthcare provider before taking any supplement.

## When to Consult a Clinician about Omega-3 and DHA Supplements
You should consult a clinician about Omega-3 and DHA supplements if:
* You're pregnant and want to supplement with Omega-3 and DHA
* You have any underlying health conditions
* You're taking any medications

## Conclusion
Omega-3 and DHA are essential nutrients for fetal development. There are many food sources rich in these nutrients, but it's crucial to be cautious when consuming fish during pregnancy.
